The must-sees

  • Amalienborg

    Palace · 1760

    Built in the 1750s for noble families, Amalienborg became the royal home after Christiansborg burned in 1794. The Royal Life Guard is changed here every day.

    Look for: In the middle of the square, Frederik V rides a bronze horse, the king who founded this district.

  • Christiansborg

    Civic building · 1928

    This is the third Christiansborg on the islet of Slotsholmen. Ruins of the earlier castles survive in the cellars beneath it.

    Look for: In front of the palace, an equestrian statue shows Frederik VII, the king who gave Denmark its constitution in 1849.

  • Nyhavn

    Waterfront · 1673

    Nyhavn was dug in the 1670s as a merchant harbor. Sailors’ bars once lined the quay; today the painted houses are the city’s front porch.

    Look for: Find the plaques at numbers 18, 20 and 67. Hans Christian Andersen lived in all three houses.

  • Rosenborg Castle

    Palace · 1633

    Rosenborg began as a summer house in 1606 and grew into a Dutch Renaissance castle. The treasury in the basement holds the Danish crown jewels.

    Look for: In the Long Hall, the coronation throne is made of narwhal tusk and guarded by three life-size silver lions.

  • Tivoli Gardens

    Venue · 1843

    Georg Carstensen is said to have told the king that when people are amused they do not think of politics. Tivoli opened in 1843 and still mixes rides, pantomime and gardens.

    Look for: Find the old wooden roller coaster from 1914. A brakeman still rides on each train to slow it down on the drops.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Copenhagen and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Copenhagen passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
